answer.text:
On startup, Paws inspects resumable work items and recovers them according to where they were interrupted. A running item is generally resumed once in a fresh session from its checkpoint, or from its branch when no checkpoint exists; if it was already resumed once and remains unfinished, Paws asks in Linear whether to start it again rather than repeatedly resuming it. (`src/core/recovery.ts:75-106`)

Items whose runner still holds the work are not duplicated: a running item is reattached to the runner's existing command, while a verifying item re-verifies and attaches to the runner's existing Closeout review or check run. If the run was still active in Paws when the process stopped, the item re-verifies instead of merely resuming. The README likewise says that runners retain their results while Paws is down and Paws reattaches after startup, including in-flight Closeout reviews and answer tasks. (`README.md:1-75`)(`src/core/recovery.ts:75-106`)

The merge queue has a separate safety path: the item keeps its place, and Paws checks GitHub before moving it, specifically to determine whether a merge call that may have gone through before the interruption actually succeeded. The in-flight condition is durably recorded in the `merge_call` table. (`src/core/recovery.ts:75-106`)(`src/db/remote-merges.ts:78-91`) Existing capacity waits, pending-answer resumes, and pending transient retries are left in place rather than given duplicate work. (`src/db/recovery.ts:41-115`)

answer.text:
Paws recovers in-flight work on startup rather than blindly restarting it. `recoverOnStartup` examines items in `awaiting_input`, `running`, `verifying`, `recovering`, and `merge_queue`, then chooses a state-specific recovery action. (`src/db/recovery.ts:31-37`) (`src/db/recovery.ts:51-74`)

For running or recovering work, Paws normally resumes it in a fresh session from its checkpoint, or from its branch when no checkpoint exists. If the runner still holds the item, Paws resumes with reattachment to the existing command. If the item has already been resumed recently, Paws asks in Linear whether to start it again instead of automatically entering a repeated restart loop. (`src/core/recovery.ts:75-105`) (`src/core/recovery.test.ts:82-119`)

Verification work is generally re-verified rather than sent back to the agent. This applies when the checkpoint shows merge work was in progress, when a runner still holds a Closeout review or check run, or when the checkpoint contains a verification candidate. For a verifying item whose runner still holds the work, startup avoids creating another re-verification job when an open re-verification is already pending, allowing that existing work to continue. (`src/core/recovery.ts:94-105`) (`src/db/recovery.ts:65-86`)

Merge-queued work keeps its place in the merge queue. If its run is still active, it is re-verified before merging. If a GitHub merge call may have been in flight, the startup decision records that condition and the merge job first asks GitHub whether the merge succeeded. (`src/core/recovery.ts:75-82`) (`src/core/recovery.ts:95-97`) (`src/db/remote-merges.ts:78-80`) (`src/core/recovery.test.ts:122-141`)

Paws also leaves already-scheduled work alone: items with a parked capacity wait, a pending answer resume, or a pending transient retry are skipped during startup, preserving their existing next attempt. New resume jobs are staggered by five seconds rather than restarting all recovered work simultaneously. (`src/db/recovery.ts:62-64`) (`src/db/recovery.ts:84-86`) (`src/db/recovery.ts:39`)

Items waiting for input have their run capacity released, and Paws queues a catch-up job to handle their open questions. (`src/db/recovery.ts:89-98`) The deployment documentation also says runners may continue working while Paws is down and that Paws reattaches to the same commands after startup, including in-flight Closeout reviews and answer tasks. (`README.md:52-55`)
